title: Near-Extremal Black Hole Entropy Yields Logarithmic Corrections in Massive
excerpt: A theoretical study demonstrates that boundary graviton zero-modes generate logarithmic corrections to the semiclassical entropy of near-extremal black holes in three-dimensional massive gravity.
content:
Theoretical physicists have determined that the one-loop partition function generates logarithmic corrections to the semiclassical entropy of near-extremal black holes in three-dimensional massive gravity. The investigation provides a new extension to higher-curvature gravity of results recently obtained for near-extremal black holes in General Relativity.

The study focused on three-dimensional massive gravity at a special point where the theory exhibits a unique maximally symmetric vacuum. At this specific point, non-constant curvature hairy black holes are capable of achieving extremality even in the static case.

To evaluate the quantum corrections, the researchers analyzed the near-horizon AdS2 × S1 geometry of the black holes. Within this background, the investigation evaluated the specific contributions of boundary graviton modes.

The calculations demonstrated that these boundary graviton modes become exact zero-modes in the extremal limit. By accounting for these zero-modes, the resulting one-loop partition function directly accounts for logarithmic corrections to the semiclassical black hole entropy.
